modem.status.note: 00 00 (idle). Sent with fn_send / raw_frame, read with fn_raw / raw_get: two bare bytes, no frame (rs232.cpp:381-386)

modem.stream.note: 28 A0 00 A0 28 A0 00 A0 78: modemBaud starts at 115200, which STREAM does not know, so the 19200 table (modem.cpp:315-351)

modem.configure.note: no bytes at all; modemBaud = 9600 whatever is asked (modem.cpp:250-256)

modem.stream.9600.note: 56 A0 00 A0 56 A0 00 A0 78 after CONFIGURE

modem.baudratelock.note: fields 1, 2400 as two u16 (F_B12_B34); the later CONNECTs say 2400

modem.set_dump.note: field 0 (sniffer off); the field is required

modem.write.at.trap: AT result text is never sent: cmdOutput is false for the whole command (modem.cpp:105, 113, 468-525). Confirmed: no OK, no bytes at all

modem.write.note: ATDT127.0.0.1:7801<CR> in a WRITE: no OK/Connecting text; the board's 106-byte greeting arrives at once, then 'CONNECT 2400' CR LF about 1 s later (ANSWER_TIMER_MS, modem.cpp:1427-1440)
modem.write.surprise: the far end's data reaches the H89 BEFORE the CONNECT result: TCP data is forwarded on every pass while CONNECT waits ANSWER_TIMER_MS (modem.cpp:1427-1440 vs 1498-1516). fwspec does not say so

modem.write.online.note: online, the WRITE payload goes to TCP (modem.cpp:115-119): the board echoes 'hello' and sends CR LF 'HELLO' CR LF '> '

modem.write.plus.trap: +++ escape is dead (plusCount only counted under #ifdef OBSOLETE, modem.cpp:1442-1491, 1521-1533): the three bytes go to the board, which echoes 2B 2B 2B; no OK after 2 s of quiet

modem.write.ath.trap: so ATH online is data: the board answers CR LF '+++ATH' CR LF '> ' (it saw '+++ATH' as one line); the call stays up

modem.write.bye.note: BYE to the board: 'Goodbye.', the board hangs up, the modem sends 'NO CARRIER' CR LF (modem.cpp:1536-1571)

modem.write.raw_dial.note: the same ATDT as bare bytes outside any frame (rs232.cpp:99-109 -> rs232Modem::tx -> rs232_write): greeting, then CONNECT 2400, as with the WRITE. The H89's bare bytes are in tap.jsonl as {dir: h89, raw} records; mkexamples.py keeps only fn-side raw bytes, so this key has no request strip

modem.write.raw_bye.note: bare BYE<CR> while online goes to the board: Goodbye., NO CARRIER

modem.listen.note: LISTEN 7803 (one u16 field); the rig's helper connects about 0.3 s later and the modem sends 'RING' CR LF (then every 3 s)

modem.write.ata.note: exactly 'ATA' CR as the payload sets answerHack (modem.cpp:103-114, 1317-1324); then the caller's PING CR LF and CONNECT 2400 CR LF
modem.write.ata.surprise: ATA alone does produce output: a bare CR LF (0D 0A) comes first. The answerHack path runs modemCommand() from the service loop with cmdOutput true, so the command echo's at_cmd_println() (modem.cpp:1039-1040) is sent; fwspec says AT output is suppressed on both input paths

modem.write.pong.note: PONG goes to the caller (helpers.jsonl logs it), which hangs up: NO CARRIER CR LF

modem.write.atcpm.note: ATCPM: SYSTEM_BUS.getCPM() is nullptr on this build (modem.cpp:1254-1258; rs232.h:159), fujinet-pc crashes. Snippet written, never run

modem.listen.port0.note: LISTEN 0: transaction_error() then transaction_success() -> assert(state) fails (modem.cpp:372-380; rs232.cpp:55). Snippet written, never run

modem.status.nofield.note: STATUS without its field: param(0) .at() throws, fujinet-pc terminates (modem.cpp:1648)

modem.write.badport.note: ATDT host:abc (non-numeric port): std::stoi throws -> abort (modem.cpp:861)
